per_view_vs_shared_neighborhood: Ting K. M. SCoNE: Spherical Consistent Neighborhoods Ensemble for Effective and Efficient Multi-View Anomaly Detection. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 40(19): 16083-16090
column10: States the core problem of multi-view anomaly detection to be representing local neighborhoods of normal instances consistently across all views; notes that recent approaches represent the local neighborhood in each view independently and then capture the consistent neighbors across all views by a learning process, and that this can fail when the same neighbors sit in regions of different density across views; SCoNE instead represents the consistent neighborhoods with multi-view instances directly, without learning, giving O(N) cost.
column11: Both alternatives are named explicitly: per-view independent neighborhood representations that are later reconciled, versus a consistent neighborhood represented directly.
column12: The shared-versus-independent neighbourhood choice is already an established research axis in multi-view anomaly detection, so the operation itself cannot be claimed as new. What remains specific here is the frozen-encoder few-shot localisation setting with pixel-level evaluation, the isolation of effective weight from added representation, and the paired interaction estimate with uncertainty.

what_it_establishes: Jiang Y. Multi-View Anomaly Detection: Neighborhood in Locality Matters. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 33(01): 4894-4901
column9: Proposes a nearest-neighbour-based multi-view anomaly detection approach; separates view-inconsistent anomalies (dissension) from anomalies that are consistently anomalous in every view (unanimous); formulates the objective to estimate the set of normal instances explicitly rather than only profiling them.
column10: Neighbourhood structure is treated per view and then related across views; the anomaly types are defined by whether the cross-view neighbourhood relations agree.
column11: Confirms that per-view neighbourhood versus cross-view agreement is a studied distinction. The present work differs in that the reference set is the few-shot normal support of an industrial image class, the branches are frozen pretrained encoders, and the question asked is whether the *benefit of adding a branch* depends on the matching rule.

evidence_level: Liu X. Neighborhood Consensus Networks for Unsupervised Multi-view Outlier Detection. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
column9: Encodes intrinsic information of each view and then uniforms the neighbourhood structures among different views, i.e. enforces a consensus neighbourhood across views.
column10: Explicitly the consensus (shared) direction: neighbourhood structure is unified across views.
column11: Another established instance of cross-view neighbourhood consistency; cited so that the related-work section does not rest only on industrial-inspection papers.

per_view_vs_shared_neighborhood: Duan L. Learning Enhanced Representations via Contrasting for Multi-view Outlier Detection. DASFAA 2023
column10: Uses neighborhood consistency to uniform the neighbourhood structures among different views, and reports an outlier score function for different outlier types.
column11: Shared/consensus neighbourhood direction again, stated as a design mechanism.
column12: Supporting citation for the same axis; not an industrial few-shot localisation work.
